---
title: "How suggestions become edits"
---

Every suggestion has a public GitHub page. That's where the editor asks questions, records a decision and links to the resulting edits. You can follow the whole discussion there.

## Reviewing the idea

The editor checks whether the handbook already covers the question, whether the advice needs evidence and which pages would need to change. Sometimes a suggestion needs a little more detail. Sometimes it belongs with an existing discussion.

The outcome may be acceptance for drafting, a request for evidence, deferral, decline or a link to a duplicate suggestion. The editor records the reason so you can understand the decision and respond.

## Reviewing the draft

An accepted suggestion goes to a contributor or an AI agent with an agreed scope. They prepare edits in a **pull request**, GitHub's name for a proposed change. The request shows the changed text, supporting sources and checks.

An authorised editor then reads the actual edits and asks for revisions, accepts them for publication or rejects them. Accepting an idea gives permission to draft; publication follows this second review. The original suggestion links to the published result.

## Editorial roles

Reviewers can check evidence, ask questions and recommend changes. Editors handle suggestions and draft reviews. Project leads manage publishing permissions and appoint additional editors as the project grows.

The current automation restricts approval and decline commands to the founding editor's GitHub account. Adding an editorial role in these pages does not grant account access. Any future editors who can approve work or publish changes must be explicitly authorised in the repository settings and workflow.

## Working with an agent

An authorised `/approve` comment, or the `decision: approved` label, starts the assignment workflow. When the Copilot credential and account access are available, Copilot prepares a pull request. An assignment failure is recorded on the suggestion so an editor can check it or assign the work manually.

An editor can also give Codex an approved issue URL with this instruction: `Implement this approved handbook issue and return a tested pull request. Do not merge it.` The agent checks the approval and supporting evidence before drafting.

See the [tracker guide](tracker.qmd) to interpret the labels attached to a suggestion.
